statement: corpus drift silently invalidating prior reflection digests and candidate stamps is prevented by fingerprint comparison at check-time
mechanism: additive ingestion changes .graph_fingerprint; check-time mismatch forces guarded re-stamping (check_reflection.py --replan) or quarantine
limitation: re-stamp can deadlock on big additive changes; mitigation verifies cited IDs before stamp update

statement: cross-platform byte divergence (CRLF vs LF) invalidates provenance on clean clones; the fingerprint was the detector that exposed this defect class
mechanism: noble-workspace: incident 2026-09-21 in CONTEXT.md daily handoff (fc0231 vs ad2962 per checkout, fixed via .gitattributes eol=lf)

statement: the fingerprint does not prevent wrong-but-stable corpora: a bad chunk that builds cleanly still stamps fine
mechanism: noble: fingerprint is a drift detector (state equality), not a truth detector; content validation is out of its scope
limitation: absence claim — no observed incident cited

statement: ingestion-time defects (double-ingested sources, boilerplate chunk titles) are not prevented or detected by the fingerprint
mechanism: noble: empirically observed in this study — 00_06/01_06 dual prefixes and 01_new_markdown_file both carry valid fingerprints
limitation: scope of provenance rule, not a corpus claim
